_source: Deterministic TTS preprocessing rules, the spoken-register rulebook, and a respelling list for TTS.
_usage: Written -> spoken Dhivehi for text-to-speech. These are reading rules, not spelling rules: never write the spoken forms back into text.

atoll_codes._rule: An atoll code written with a full stop before a place name (ބ. ތުޅާދޫ, ބ.އަތޮޅު) is read as the letter name(s). Match two-letter codes first so ހއ. is not read as ހ + އ.

fixed_substitutions.note: ligature expanded to the recited phrase
rufiyaa marker, e.g. 4.72ރ. (numbers are spelled out separately)
trailing stop after the title is not a sentence end

spoken_register_endings._rule: Written Dhivehi ends sentences and clauses with the formal literary suffix -ެވެ (އެވެ / ށެވެ / ނެވެ / ކެވެ ...), which is not said in speech. In the spoken register each is replaced with the natural spoken form of the same word; nothing else in the sentence changes. This needs grammar, so it is handed to a language model as a rulebook with these examples; it is not a regex.

respellings._rule: Phonetic respellings offered to a TTS voice as an alternative to the standard spelling, so the voice says the sound rather than the letters. Both spellings are tried and the better take is kept. Never use them in written text.
